title: R' Nechunya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Chullin 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.55b) he said: “I asked all the experts in the laws of trefot (those who rule on the laws of animals unfit for consumption) in the West, and they told me: the halakhah follows Rekhish bar Pappa, and the halakhah does not follow Rav Avira in the name of Rava.” (Apparently he was one of the sages who went down from the Land of Israel to Babylonia toward the end of the time of Abaye and Rava.) This R' Nechunya is mentioned in [Bava Kamma 50a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.50a): “Rabbi Nechunya said: from here,” etc.[^1]

notes.text: The gloss explaining the experts in trefot and the parenthetical historical inference are Hyman’s own. The inference remains qualified as “apparently.” א״י and ב״ק are the ordinary contextual abbreviations for the Land of Israel and Bava Kamma. The printed locators נה: and נ. are rendered as 55b and 50a by the conventional colon/period notation; the matching Hebrew paragraphs have now been checked in the William Davidson vocalized Aramaic edition. The supplied attribution “in the name of Rava” is retained as Hyman’s wording, rather than added to the checked Chullin 55b paragraph.

The Chullin paragraph names רַב נְחוּנְיָא, Rav Nechunya, whereas the Bava Kamma quotation has רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא, Rabbi Nechunya. The heading and Hyman’s linking statement retain R'; the full title inside the Bava Kamma quotation follows that paragraph. Hyman associates the two references, but the title difference is preserved and does not by itself establish that every occurrence names the same person. Rav Avira retains Hyman’s explicit רב.
